paras: A survey of the evolution of dance as both ritual and art. Extensive viewing of films as well as lectures and workshop sessions. No dance background necessary.
a

paras: An in-depth examination, practical and theoretical, of the formal and thematic components of dance. Studio sessions deat with problem solving in space, dynamics and rhythm. No dance background necessary.

paras: History and cultural significance of dance up to and including Fokine and Duncan.

courses.label: DANCE 232
courses.title: Survey of Ballet History
paras: This course examines the development of ballet from the Renaissance to contemporary times, focusing on the nature of dance of the past and its changes within a cultural context. Major personalities, events and forms, as well as social influences are assessed for their impact on the art.
Not for Dance Majors

paras: This course examines the major choreographic innovators, who have philosophicaily and stylistically shaped the modern dance idiom.
Prereq: DANCE 230
Offered alternate years

courses.title: Women in Western Theatre Dance
paras: The achievements of women in. dance will be viewed in the context of the woman's place in artistic and social hierarchies, as well as in the light of the disadvantages and advantages experienced due to being female. Autobiographies, biographies, films, videos, and historical accounts will be consulted.

Introductory Notes
1, EARTH 121/122 is normally regarded as a prerequisite for any Major program in Earth Sciences.

2. Second, third and fourth year courses may invalve field trips in the fall. All those enrolled in Honours Earth Sciences programs are required to take a two-week field camip at the end of the third year (EARTH 390). The cost will range from $50-$100 per student.
3. Regular Earth Sciences students are encouraged to seek geological employment in the summers.

courses.label: EARTH 121
courses.title: Introductory Geology 1
paras: An introduction to rocks and minerals and the processes of their formation. The structure of the earth, plate tectonics and its relationship to deformation, metamorphism and formation of magmas. Earth resources.

courses.label: EARTH 122
courses.title: Introductory Geology 2
paras: An introduction to processes that shape the earth’s landscapes. Consideration of the time concept in geology. Introduction to fossils, their occurrence and uses in earth sciences. The geological history of North America.
Prereq: EARTH 121

courses.label: EARTH 221
courses.title: Geochemistry 1
paras: Origin, abundance and geochemistry of elements. Introduction to stable isotope geology and radiometric dating. Basic aqueous geochemistry. Chemica! characteristics of crystalline and sedimentary rocks.
Prereq: EARTH 231 or permission of instructor

courses.label: EARTH 231
courses.title: Mineralogy
paras: Introduction to systematic mineralogy. Bases of mineral classification. Interretationships of chemical, structural and physical properties. Occurrence of major groups of rock-forming minerals. Introduction to optical properties of minerats and the use of the petrographic microscope as a tool in identifying minerals and interpreting their genetic history. Prereq: EARTH 121

courses.label: EARTH 232
courses.title: Petrography
paras: The study of rocks in thin section. The classification and identification of sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic rocks.
Prereq: EARTH 231

courses.label: EARTH 235
courses.title: Stratigraphy
paras: An introduction to the nature, origin and interpretation of stratified earth materials. Emphasis on principles and approaches. Stratigraphy in earth history and economic deposits.
Prereq: EARTH 121/122

courses.label: EARTH 236
courses.title: Principles of Paleontology
paras: The principles of paleontology with
particular stress on the species concept
and evolution; examples will be drawn
primarily from the fossil record of plants
and vertebrates. Laboratory work will
include projects related to lecture topics. Prereq: EARTH 121/122

courses.label: EARTH 238
courses.title: Introductory Structura! Geology
paras: Major structural features of the earth. Concepts of stress and strain; elementary rock mechanics. The deformation of earth materiats, continuous and discontinuous structures. Introduction to regional tectonics.
Prereq: EARTH 121/122

courses.label: EARTH 260
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 1
paras: An introduction to seismic, gravity, elec-
tric, electromagnetic and magnetic
methods of exploration geophysics. Prereq: PHYS 111/112 or consent of
instructor

courses.label: EARTH 331
courses.title: Igneous Petrology
paras: The principles and theories of igneous rock genesis. Silicate phase equilibria in magmatic systems. Magmatic differentiation; distribution and occurrence of magma types.
Prereq: EARTH 231, 232

courses.label: EARTH 332
courses.title: Metamorphic Petrology
paras: Principles and theories of metamorphic rock genesis. Static, dynamic and polyphasal crystalloblastic growth. Processes of solid-state crystallization in metamorphic environments. Zonal and facies classifications; facies series and the place of metamorphism in global tectonics. Introduction to metasomatism.
Prereq: EARTH 232.
For Honours Earth Sciences and Geological Engineering students only.

courses.label: EARTH 333
courses.title: Introductory Sedimentology
paras: The origin, transport and deposition of sediments. Size analysis and sedimentary structures. Recent sedimentary environments as a key to the interpretation of ancient sediments. Sedimentary petrology. ‘
Prereq: EARTH 232

courses.label: EARTH 336
courses.title: Paleontology
paras: Advanced paleontology emphasizing morphology, classification, evolution, paleoecology and stratigraphic value of fossil invertebrates. Laboratory study of fossil collections.
Prereq: EARTH 236

courses.label: EARTH 342
courses.title: Geomorphology
paras: The process of landscape evolution and the classification of landforms. Geomorphic effects of glacial, fluvial, marine and slope processes. Physicat and chemical weathering, soil formation. Laboratory study of topographic maps and air photo interpretation. Field trips. Antireq: GEOG 201

courses.label: EARTH 345
courses.title: Historical Geology
paras: A systematic review of the geological history of North America from the Precambrian to the Recent exemplified by regional geology. Laboratory work will include study of rocks and fossil regional suites and geological maps.
Prereq: EARTH 235

courses.label: EARTH 355
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Geology
paras: Introduction to the principles of probability and statistics and their application in the earth sciences. Evaluation of quantitative data; statistical models.
Prereq: MATH 113A/B and an introductory course in computer programming

courses.label: EARTH 358
courses.title: Environmental Geology
paras: The influence of geology on the natural environment with special emphasis on hazards and the role of groundwater; hydrogeology in the runoff cycle; groundwater resources development and subsurface waste disposal; environ: mental geology as a factor in health and disease. Prereq: EARTH 121/122 or GEO E 126 Antireq: SCI 250

courses.label: EARTH 360A
courses.title: Global Geophysics
paras: Topics in the plate tectonics, heat flow.
gravity, seismology, magnetics, electro-
magnetics and dynamics of the planet. Prereq: PHYS 121/122, EARTH 260 Offered every other year alternating
with EARTH 460.

courses.label: EARTH 368
courses.title: Geophysics 1
paras: Introductory topics on the physics of the earth. Seismology and the earth’s interior. Thermal history of the earth. Gravity and isostasy. Origin of the continents and continental drift. . Prereg: MATH 113A/B, PHYS 121/122 or equivalent Cross-listed as PHYS 368

courses.label: EARTH 369
courses.title: Geophysics 2
paras: The geology of the ocean basins. Topics in physical oceanography. Physical properties of ocean water, heat budget of the world oceans. Oceanic circulation, Coriolis effects, Some idealized current regimes.
Prereq: MATH 113A4/B and PHYS 121/122 or equivalent
Cross-listed as PHYS 369

courses.label: EARTH 370
courses.title: Economic Geology
paras: The occurrence and geological setting of metallic, non-metallic minerals and construction materials. Energy resources. Special emphasis on Canada’s resource industries. The laboratory will involve sampling methods, ore calculation and property evaluation.
Prereq: EARTH 231, 232

courses.label: EARTH 390
courses.title: Methods in Geological Mapping
paras: Ten day field camp at Whitefish Falls, held at beginning of spring term.

courses.label: EARTH 421
courses.title: Geochemistry 2
paras: The application of chemical thermodynamics to geochemical problems. Development of the three laws of Thermodynamics; Gibbs free energy and equilibria constants. introduction to various topics in aqueous geochemistry such as mineral equilibria, ion exchange and redox equilibria. Various aspects of organic geochemistry and geochemical expioration will also be covered.
Prereq: First year chemistry, EARTH 221
Restricted to fourth year and graduate students. °

courses.label: EARTH 427
courses.title: Crustal Evolution
paras: An analytical critique of the plate tectonics theory. Tectonic syntheses based on the theory in the light of world geology.
Normally restricted to fourth year Earth Sciences students.

courses.label: EARTH 432
courses.title: Precambrian Geology
paras: The geology, tectonics, stratigraphy and history of the Canadian Precambrian Shield. The early evolution of the earth’s crust. The Precambrian time scale and problems of geochronology. Life, climate and physical conditions in Precambrian time.

courses.label: EARTH 433
courses.title: Applied Sedimentology
paras: The source, migration and sedimentary environment of hydrocarbons, exploration, types of traps, extraction. Carbonate sediments and their diagenesis. The environmental impact and control of recent sedimentation.
Prereq: EARTH 333

courses.label: EARTH 434
courses.title: Biostratigraphy
paras: Methods of using paleontological data to solve stratigraphic problems. Faunal provinces in space and time. Effects of continenta! drift and climatic change on biogeography through the Phanerozoic. Prereq: EARTH 336

courses.label: EARTH 435
courses.title: Advanced Structural Geology
paras: The geometry, kinematics and dynamics of structural geology. The relationships of structures from the microscopic to the megascopic scale; statistical studies of structural elements.
Prereq: EARTH 260

courses.label: EARTH 436A
courses.title: Honours Thesis
paras: (A course for Honours Earth Sciences students only.) Each student will work under the direction of a member of the Department on a short research project. The results of this will be presented in thesis form and will be critically examined by members of this and, where pertinent, other departments.

courses.label: EARTH 437
courses.title: Rock Mechanics
paras: Review of stress and strain. Mohr's circle, strength theories, laboratory tests, classification of rocks. Rock mechanics considerations in the construction of shafts, drifts, tunnels, foundations and rock slopes. Laboratory exercises will deal with uniaxial, triaxial, flexure, hardness and tensile testing of rock. Problem sets will be assigned.
Prereq: A course in Statics and Mechanics of deformable materials, or consent of instructor

courses.label: EARTH 438
courses.title: Engineering Geology
paras: Review of basic concepts in soil and tock mechanics. Field and taboratory methods used to define and characterize the properties of geological materials and their use in selected engineering geologic design and construction problems. Laboratory assignments will focus on the determination of physical properties and site assessment problems.

courses.label: EARTH 440
courses.title: Quaternary Geology Stratigraphy and history of the Quater-
paras: nary Period with emphasis on glaciation. Laboratory studies on glacial deposits. Field trios. A previous course in geomorphology is recommended. Antireq: for students majoring in Earth Sciences: GEOG 300 and GEOG 401 Not to be taken by third year students.

courses.label: EARTH 456
courses.title: Numerical Methods in Geoscience
paras: introduction to numerical methods and their use in geology and hydrogeoiogy. Finite differences and finite elements. Solution of boundary value problems, mathematical modelling.
Prereq: MATH 113A/B and an introductory course in computer programming

courses.label: EARTH 458
courses.title: Physical Hydrogeology
paras: An introduction to the physical side of © hydrogeology, including Darcy's law, the groundwater flow equations far steadystate and transient conditions, applications to flow nets, aquifer testing, groundwater resources evaluation, and construction-project dewatering. The role of groundwater in the hydrologic cycle is explored with emphasis on natural groundwater flow systems and their influence on stream flow, slope stability and soil drainage.
Prereq: EARTH 121/122 or GEO E 126 or CIV E 283, and MATH 213A/B or equivalents.
Formerly EARTH 439

courses.label: EARTH 459
courses.title: Chemical Hydrogeology
paras: An introduction to the chemical side of hydrogeology with emphasis on groundwater quality and contaminants in the groundwater zone, the geochemical origin of major ions in natural groundwater, causes of hardness, groundwater age determination using isotopes, common causes of groundwater contamination; processes governing contaminant behaviour including dispersion, diffusion and adsorption, hydrogeologic aspects of site selection for waste disposal.
Prereq: EARTH 221 or CIV E 375 or equivatent, and EARTH 458
Formerly EARTH 439

courses.label: EARTH 460
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 2
paras: A detailed examination of selected topics in exploration geophysics, with an emphasis on data processing and computer modelling of geophysical responses. Prereq: EARTH 260 and an introductory course in computer programming Offered every other year alternating with EARTH 360A

courses.label: EARTH 461
courses.title: Applied Geophysics 3
paras: Geophysical field methods for Engineering and Hydrogeology.
Prereq: Students must be enrolled in the Geophysics Option

courses.label: EARTH 470
courses.title: Metallic Mineral Deposits
paras: The petrology and genesis of metalliferous ore deposits. The description of classic deposits; the stability of ore minerals; ore minerals in aqueous systems. The laboratory will include instruction and practice in ore microscopy.
Prereq: EARTH 370

courses.label: EARTH 480
courses.title: Field Study
paras: Depending on the demand and the availability of an instructor, a six week field course may be offered in an area of unusual geological interest during the spring or summer. This course will consist of two weeks of classroom lectures and one month in the field location. Expenses are to be paid by the student. Prereq: Consent of the instructor

courses.label: EARTH 490
courses.title: Field Trip
paras: One or more regional geology field trips normally conducted at the beginning of the Fall term. These trips will emphasize the.integration of the various subdiscipfines within Geology to achieve an understanding and synthesis of a geologically complex region such as the central and western Appalachians of southern Quebec. Field exercises will be part of the trip. Enrolment will be limited to not more than 30 students per trip.
Open to Honours Earth Sciences Students only.

courses.label: ECON 102
courses.title: Introduction to Macroeconomics
paras: Determination of national income; the banking system; government fiscal and monetary policy; international trade and finance; and current economic problems.

courses.label: ECON 201

paras: Theory of consumer choice; the economits of production; pricing and output under perfect and imperfect competition.
Prereq: ECON 101

courses.label: ECON 202
courses.title: Macroeconomic Theory
paras: Theory of the determination of the level of national income (GNP), the unemployment rate, interest rates, prices and inflation; analysis of macroeconomic policies to stabilize the economy and alleviate the problems of inflation and unemployment. Prereq: ECON 101, 102

courses.label: ECON 211
courses.title: Mathematics of Economists
paras: Application of mathematics to problems in economic theory. Topics include an introduction to matrix algebra, differentiation, partial derivatives, optimization techniques including constrained optimization - all developed within the context of economic theory. .
Prereq: ECON 101, 102
Students who have not taken Grade 13 Algebra and Calculus are strongly advised to take MATH 104.

courses.label: ECON 221
courses.title: Statistics for Economists
paras: An introduction to statistical procedures commonly employed by economists. Topics inctude descriptive statistics, probability distributions, statistical estimation, hypothesis testing and regression analysis.
Prereq: ECON 101, 102

concepts and measurement of balance
of payments; exchange rate systems.

paras: Methods for evaluating private and _ public projects; decision rules, efficiency conditions and methods of conducting cost-benefit analysis. Application of the technique.

Canada; development theories, industrial

paras: Monetary theory and banking in an open
economy; national policies for achieving
full employment, price stability, and equi-
librium in the balance of payments Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Economics
paras: Mathematical treatment of some microand macro-partial and general equilibrium models; programming and other techniques; simple growth modeis.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 211 (or MATH 130B)

courses.label: ECON 321

paras: Introductory level course in econometrics; includes economic model building and testing, regression and correlation analysis, and price indices.
Prereq: ECON 221

courses.label: ECON 331
courses.title: International Trade and Finance
paras: An examination of theories of intemational trade and finance at an intermediate level. Topics include theories of trade structure (Ricardian, Heckscher- Ohlin), the effects of tariffs and multinational corporation behaviours, and adjustment under flexible and fixed exchange rates.
Prereq: ECON 201, 231

courses.label: ECON 333
courses.title: Interregional Economics
paras: An examination of structural characteristics, development and growth in intersystems. Prereq: ECON 201, 231

courses.label: ECON 335
courses.title: Economic Development
paras: The nature of the problem of economic development; theories of economic development; major policy issues in economic development.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202, 231

courses.label: ECON 341
courses.title: Public Finance
paras: The economic rationale of governmental fiscal activity; cost-benefit analysis; the structure and economic effects of public expenditure and revenues; the analysis of income, consumption and wealth taxes.
Prereq: ECON 102, 201

courses.label: ECON 343
courses.title: Urban Economics
paras: Application of economic analysis to urban and metropolitan areas. Topics include location decisions of households and firms, structure and growth of cities, land and housing market, urban transportation market, urban labour market, and urban public finance - all developed within the context of economic theory. Policy issues will be stressed.
Prereq: ECON 101
(ECON 201 is recommended)

courses.label: ECON 344
courses.title: Consumer Theory
paras: Economic principles for consumer analysis; market responsiveness; conditions causing problems; public and private consumption; alternative economic policies.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 345
courses.title: Industrial Organization
paras: An economic analysis of market structure, behaviour and performance with special reference to the Canadian manufacturing sector.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 351
courses.title: Labour Economics
paras: A study of the supply of labour by individuals and the demand for labour by firms; investment in human capital; trade unions; internal labour markets.
Prereq: ECON 201
ECON 102 is recommended

courses.label: ECON 353
courses.title: Population Economics
paras: Population objectives; demographic tech-
niques; economic interrelationships with fertility, mortality and migration; determinants and consequences of current world population changes.
Prereq: ECON 201

courses.label: ECON 355
courses.title: Economics of Energy and Natural Resources
paras: An analysis of the economics of conservation, especially the adequacy of the market mechanism as an allocator of resource use over time. Issues concerning the economic behaviour of «. Canada’s fishery, forest, fuel and nonfuel mineral industries will be considered. Prereq: ECON 201 (ECON 241 is recommended.)

courses.label: ECON 363
courses.title: Contemporary Canadian Problems 1,2
paras: A “topic oriented” seminar course. Problems are selected from a list that includes regulatory economics, poverty, unemployment, industrial policy, safety and so forth. The format assists the student in gaining analytical skill through work on the selected topics.
Prereq: ECON 201, 202

courses.label: ECON 365
courses.title: Economic Development of Modern

courses.label: ELE 123
courses.title: Electrical Engineering Circuits
paras: Introduction to network variables; resis- * tors; Kirchhoff's laws; circuit simplification techniques; circuit analysis methods; operational amplifiers and their uses; resistor-capacitor circuits; resistorinductor circuits; sinusoids and phasors; impedance and admittance; circuit functions and analysis techniques.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 126
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electrostatics; electric flux and potential energy; dielectrics, capacitors and capacitance; flow of electric charge and resistance; Kirchhoff’s Voltage and Current Laws; magnetism; magnetic materials and circuits; Faraday’s Law and inductance.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 205
courses.title: Advanced Calculus for Electrical Engineers 1 Fourier Series; Ordinary differential equa-
paras: tions; Laplace transform; applications to linear electrical systems.

courses.label: ELE 206
courses.title: Advanced Caiculus for Electrical Engineers 2
paras: Partial differentiation, relative maxima and minima, directional derivatives, diver-
gence and curl of vector fields with appli-

cations; multiple integrals, double and triple integrals; line and surface integrais, applications of divergence and Stokes theorems. Complex analysis: limits, analytic functions, complex line integral, Cauchy's integral formula, residues. Partial differential equations.
Cross-listed as MATH 212

courses.label: ELE 208
courses.title: Electronic Circuit Analysis
paras: This is an introductory course in electronic circuit analysis which follows the first circuits course EL E 123. The topics to be discussed are: Operational! amplifier applications, diodes, rectifiers, introduction to MOS and bipolar transistors, basic amplifier circuits, frequency response, elementary treatments of feedback, filters and oscillators. The student is introduced to computer-aided analysis techniques using WATAND.
Prereq: EL E 123 or equivalent
Antireq: EL E 234
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 222
courses.title: Digital Computers
paras: Brief introduction to switching algebra. Information representation and arithmetic in binary systems. Computer organization. Assembly language programming, basic programming techniques. Memory units, arithmetic logic units, control units, VO devices. Translation and loading. Computer case studies. Microcomputers. Prereq: GEN E 121 or equivalent Open

courses.label: ELE 224
courses.title: Numerical Methods
paras: Application of computers to engineering problems. Number systems, errors and error propagation. Roots of nonlinear equations. Solution of systems of linear equations. interpolation and numerical integration. Solution of ordinary differential equations. A non-numeric algorithm (e.g. sorting). Emphasis will be placed on algorithm development and programming style.
Prereq: GEN E 121 or equivalent

courses.label: ELE 231
courses.title: Electronic Devices
paras: Review of band theory and doped semiconductors in thermal equilibrium, charge neutrality, mass action law, recombination and transport mechanisms, Boltzmann relations, derivation of p-n junction de and ac characteristics, charge storage effects. The bipolar transistor; derivation of de and ac: terminal characteristics, equivalent circuits. The Junction Fieid Effect transistor (FET) and Metal Oxide Semiconductor FET, derivation of de characteristics. Prereq: PHYS 125.or equivalent Alternate weeks.

courses.title: Energy Systems and Components 1
paras: Comparative and historical review of energy sources and systems. Operating, security and planning principles for the electric energy generation, transmission and distribution systems. Excitation and loss analysis of ac magnetic circuits. Principles, circuit modelling, and performance of transformers. Electromechanical energy conversions. ; Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 262
courses.title: Energy Systems and Components 2
paras: Principles of electromechanical energy conversion. Rotating machines. OC motors. Induction motors. Synchronous machines.
Prereq: ElE 261

Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 316
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
paras: Conditional probability and independence; Bayes’ Theorem; random variables; functions of random variables; distribution functions; applications to reliability and failure rates; marginal and conditional distributions; correlation and applications to regression and statistical testing.

courses.label: ELE 318
courses.title: Communications Systems
paras: Orthogonality and signat representation in continuous time. Fourier spectrum, Fourier transforms and applications to communications. Convolution. Transfer functions and filters. Power spectral density. Amplitude modulation and applications to techniques such as DSB, AM, SSB, etc. Angle modulation and the spectrum of frequency modulated signals. Techniques for the generation and demodulation of FM signals. Introduction to noise and its effects in AM and FM systems. Noise figure and noise temperature.
Alternate weeks.

courses.label: ELE 323
courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
paras: Switching algebra. Simplification of Boolean functions. Combinational logic. MSI/LSI combinational circuits. Sequential logic. Algorithmic state machines, implementation with MSI circuits, timing considerations. Hardwired and microprogrammed controllers. Semiconductor memories. IC families.
Open.

courses.label: ELE 332
courses.title: Electronic Circuits
paras: Amplifier biasing networks, single and multi-stage small-signal amplifiers, the hybrid-pi model; high and low frequency effects; negative feedback amplifiers; oscillators; noise in electronic circuits; introduction to large signat amplifiers; introduction to digital circuits.
Prereq: EL E 208, EL E 231
Antireq: EL E 333
Alternate weeks

courses.label: ELE 333
courses.title: Microelectronic Circuits and Devices 2
paras: The second of a two course sequence in electronic circuits and devices. Topics covered are: device physics and models, transistor amplifier, feedback, filters and oscillators, logic circuits, memory circuits. Prereq: EL E 234 Antireq: EL E 332 Alternate weeks

paras: Transmission lines: transmission line equations, steady state (sinusoidal) solution, terminated lines, matching and the Smith Chart. courses.label: ELE 380
courses.title: Systems and Control
paras: An introduction to control. Advantages of closed-loop feedback systems. The role of the system mathematical model. Block diagrams and signal flow graphs. courses.title: Robot Dynamics and Control
paras: Homogeneous transformations. Kinematics and inverse kinematics. Denavit- Hartenberg convention. Jacobians and velocity transformations. Dynamics. Path planning, Nonlinear control. Compliance and force control. Prereq: Permission of the instructor "Project

paras: Review of sampling and pulse transmission. Signal distortion, band-width for pulse transmission. Digital multiplexing, line coding, pulse shaping, detection and error rates. {SI and equalisation. Pulsecodé modulation, Delta modulation, quantization and detection errors. Error-correcting codes: linear block codes, cyclic codes, convolution codes.

courses.label: ELE 413
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing
paras: Discrete systems for signa! processing, in particular linear filtering, are rapidly replacing analog forms. This course serves as an introduction to the analysis and design of linear, time invariant discrete systems, with both software and hardware implementations.

courses.label: ELE 426
courses.title: Software Engineering
paras: Block structured languages, actual and formal Rarameters, recursion, formal description, relationship to machine code. Compilers. courses.label: ELE 446
courses.title: Linear Systems
paras: Three types of linear multivariable systems are studied.
1. real time-continuous systems; 2. real time-discrete systems; and 3. modulo-two time-discrete systems.

Topics include: time domain analysis, transform analysis (Laplace- and Z-transforms), stability considerations, system equivafence, system decomposition, system realization. GROUP ONE

Courses in this group count towards a degree as electives in any program in the University. Normally, none of them qualifies as a major credit for a General or Honours program in English. These courses are primarily designed to make students aware of the different functions of language in various contexts and to assist them to improve their -vriting.

In order to develop clarity of thought and critical awareness, students will identify and study in several media the various ends that are served by language: objective reporting; persuasion; argument; and emotional, social, and artistic expression. About eight written exercises are assigned.

courses.label: ENGL 240R
courses.title: Form and Function 1
paras: The uses of literacy and the functions of language as acquired in ENGL 140R/141R. These will be applied to the more advanced form of the literary and critical assignment essay, involving comparison, evaluation, and exposition.
GROUP TWO
Courses in this group carry degree credit and may be counted as fulfilling the minimum requirements for a General or Honours program in English.

courses.label: ENGL 102A
courses.title: The Major Forms of Literature: Short Stories and Drama
paras: A study of short stories and drama to determine how the shape of a literary work contributes to its meaning.

courses.label: ENGL 102B
paras: The Major Forms of Literature: Novels and Poetry
A study of novels and poetry to determine how the shape of a literary work contributes to its meaning.

courses.label: ENGL 103A
courses.title: The Nature and Structure of the English Language
paras: introduction to the study of the English language. Topics to be discussed include the nature and origin of language, the structure of English and its development, and the relations between fanguage and reality.

courses.label: ENGL 103B
courses.title: Varieties of English
paras: Introduction to the study of varieties of
the English language - regional, social.
temporal, functional, and stylistic. The
relations of languages and literature and
of speech and writing will be discussed. Prereq: ENGL 103A or consent of

courses.label: ENGL 105A
courses.title: 20th-Century Literature in English
paras: A close examination of a representative selection of works by major authors writing in English such as W.B. Yeats, Virginia Woolf, D.H. Lawrence, T.S. Eliot, and Ernest Hemingway.

courses.label: ENGL 106B
courses.title: 20th-Century Literature in English
paras: A continuation of ENGL 105A. A close
examination of a representative selection
of works by major authors writing in
English such as William Faulkner, Oyian
Thomas, and Margaret Laurence. Prereq: ENGL 105A or consent of
instructor 7

courses.label: ENGL 108A
courses.title: The Hero
paras: A study of human excellence in thought
and action embodied in representative
men and women, as seen through works
of literature.

courses.label: ENGL 108E
courses.title: Women in Literature
paras: A study of the nature and role af women in British, Canadian, and American literature. Works by both men and women will be studied in which women are seen in such forms as mothers, saints, sex objects, and witches.

courses.label: ENGL 108F
courses.title: The Rebel
paras: A study of various works of literature in which the protagonist is a rebel against existing norms. The course will examine a number of rebel types and concepts, moral implications, and final outcomes either in successful realisation or in tragic defeat.

courses.label: ENGL 108H
courses.title: Isolation and Alienation
paras: The study of a variety of works centering on the theme of man in crisis, the stress being on the individual at variance with his inner self, his fellow man, or his world. The course will discuss the process in which wisdom and maturity are gained as the ultimate products of suffering

courses.label: ENGL 108M
courses.title: Youth and Adolescence
paras: Studies the portrayal of young protagonists as they respond to the mores of adult society; their own physical, mental, and psychological development; and the expectations placed upon them by themselves and by others.

courses.label: ENGL 108N
courses.title: The Wars
paras: Studies the experience of war and attitudes toward it as revealed in literary works from different historical periods.

courses.label: ENGL 190
courses.title: Shakespeare
paras: Designed for students in all faculties, the course examines some of Shakespeare’s comedies, history plays, and tragedies. Shakespeare’s variety and flexibility in developing characters and dramatic Structures are stressed, as are significant themes.
No previous work in Shakespeare is required.

courses.label: ENGL 200A
courses.title: Survey of British Literature 1
paras: An historical survey of major figures, types, and trends in British literature from the Middle Ages to the late 18th century.

courses.label: ENGL 200B
courses.title: Survey of British Literature 2
paras: An historical survey of major figures, types, and trends in British literature from the late 18th century to the present.

courses.label: ENGL 201
courses.title: The Short Story
paras: This course deals with the history and techniques of the short story, with emphasis upon works by such British, American, and Canadian writers as Henry James, James Joyce, D.H. Lawrence, Ernest Hemingway, and Alice Munro.

courses.label: ENGL 202A
courses.title: The Bible and Literature 1
paras: The study of major themes, stories, and literary characteristics of the King James Bible (Hebrew Scripture) and their influence on English jiterature.

courses.label: ENGL 202B
courses.title: The Bible and Literature 2
paras: The study of major themes, stories, and
literature characteristics of the King
James Bible (Christian Scripture) anc
their influence on English literature. Prereq: ENGL 202A or consent of
instructor

courses.label: ENGL 203
courses.title: Introduction to Folkiore 1
paras: An introduction to the scope ahd aims of folklore, together with a survey of the major types of folklore in the English tradition from nations of the Englishspeaking world. Topics such as oral literature, myth, legend, tale, and marchen will be discussed.

courses.label: ENGL 204
courses.title: Introduction to Folklore 2
paras: Similar to 203 but dealing with folkdrama, ballads, songs, medicines, tiddies, chants, proverbs, and charms.

courses.label: ENGL 205R
courses.title: The Canadian Short Story
paras: Exploration of the Canadian short story, from its beginnings ~ in the bush, in the north, on the land, in the small towns — through the struggles of an urbanizing society to the present. Students will be expected to work in some depth with individual authors.

courses.label: ENGL 208A
courses.title: Forms of Fantasy
paras: This course will deal with the history and forms of fantasy written for adults. In considering the genre, related forms like the romance, the fairy tale, the fable, and the gothic horror story will be discussed. Authors such as Morris, C.S. Lewis, Tolkien, Williams, and White will be Studied.

courses.label: ENGL 208B
courses.title: Science Fiction
paras: Various examples drawn, for instance, from Utopian and anti-Utopian science fiction, social science fiction, “gadget” science fiction, parapsychology, and alternate worlds and beings will be considered. Some attention will be given to the historical development of the genre.

courses.label: ENGL 208C
courses.title: Studies in Children’s Literature
paras: This course will deal with classic works of children’s literature, including fantasy written primarily for children. Selections from such authors as Kipling, Woolf, C.S. Lewis, George MacDonald, Kenneth Grahame, and Thurber will be studied.

courses.label: ENGL 208D
courses.title: Modern Satire
paras: The mode of satire in the fiction, drama, poetry, and discourse of the 20th century. Particular attention to the literary works of Waugh, Huxley, Orwell, Parker, Heller, Hiebert, and a dramatist of the absurd, but also attention to satiric cartoons and nightclub satire.

courses.label: ENGL 208E
courses.title: Women Writers of the 20th Century
paras: A study of such major 20th-century writers as Woolf, Hellman, Murdoch, McCarthy, Lessing, Laurence, Plath, and Atwood. Emphasis will be on the concerns of these writers with the roles of women, the writer’s search for new
Meanings, and their innoyations in literary -
forms.

courses.label: ENGL 208F
courses.title: The Literature of Aging
paras: This course will focus on literary works that present various aspects of aging, such as changes in physical and mental abilities, relationships with children and grandchildren, coping with disease and death, and the satisfactions unique to the elderly.

courses.label: ENGL 208H
courses.title: Arthurian Legend
paras: The story of Arthur and his knights of the Round Table will be discussed as it is treated at various times in various works and genres. Such matters will be considered as the character of Arthur, the concept of Camelot, and the Fellowship of the Round Table.

courses.label: ENGL 208K
courses.title: Detective Fiction
paras: The history and characteristics of the “detective novel,” the “novel of crime,” and the “thriller.” Attention will also be given to the novel of intrigue and espionage. Such authors as Poe, Collins, Doyle, Chesterton, Hammett, Buchan, Greene, Deighton, and Le Carré will be discussed. The course includes the examination of critical approaches to the form of detective fiction.
ENGL 2080 05
Ordered Chaos: The Apocalyptic Vision in Literature ‘

A study of dehumanized worlds in fiction that can be called “apocalyptic.” Works by such writers as St. John the Divine, Shakespeare, Mary Shelley, Aldous Huxley, Mordecai Richler, and Kurt Vonnegut will be studied.

courses.label: ENGL 209
courses.title: Writing Strategies
paras: Students practise effective writing along with the study of established models. The goal is to develop language competence to meet a variety of academic, business, and professional situations. Prereq: Second-year standing or above Counts as an English Major credit as of Fall. 1984.

courses.label: ENGL 210A
courses.title: Business and Technical Writing
paras: A study of the principles of business and technical writing including the styles, techniques, and forms of business and technical correspondence, application letters and résumés, abstracts, outlines, and technical description, with copious writing practice. Special attention to techniques of editing and presentation. Some practice in ora! presentation. Prereq: Second-year standing or above

courses.label: ENGL 210C
courses.title: Report Writing
paras: A study in the principles and practice of good report writing including report Janguage and styles and various forms of report organization ~ various kinds of short reports as well as the long formal research report.
Prereq: Second-year standing or above

courses.label: ENGL 211
courses.title: The Nove! 1
paras: The study of the novel written in English from its beginnings to the late 19th century.

courses.label: ENGL 212
courses.title: The Novel 2
paras: The study of the novel written in English from the late 19th century to the present.

courses.label: ENGL 214
courses.title: Themes in Canadian Literature
paras: The course will survey a theme which is significant to the understanding of the Canadian literary mind. Topics will vary from section to section.

courses.label: ENGL 219
courses.title: Contemporary Usage
paras: An in-depth, applied study of the conventions governing contemporary English grammar, punctuation, syntax, diction, spelling, and sentence structure. in addition, the course will examine variations and changes in conventions, the question of the determiners of correct usage; and the impact of dictionaries, textbooks, journals, large publishing houses, and international wire services on accepted English usage in general and on Canadian usage in particular.

courses.label: ENGL 232
courses.title: The Development of Drama to 1860
paras: A study of the origins and development of English drama, with special concentration on 16th-century non-Shakespearean drama.
Students may receive credit for only one of ENGL 232 or DRAMA 252.

courses.label: ENGL 233
paras: Drama from 1660 A study of the principal playwrights, . plays, and movements in dramatic history from the re-opening of the theatres in 1660 to the present day.
Students may receive credit for only one of ENGL 233 or DRAMA 253.

courses.label: ENGL 251A
courses.title: The Practice and Theory of Criticiem 1
paras: The study and practice of skills needed for a close, analytical reading of literary texts and for the writing of critical analyses on them; studies of theories conceming literature and literary criticisms.

courses.label: ENGL 251B
courses.title: The Practice and Theory of Criticism 2
paras: The continuation of ENGL 251A (See above).
Prereq: ENGL 251A

courses.label: ENGL 305A
courses.title: Old English 1
paras: An introduction to the English language in its earliest form and to English prose in pre-Conquest England, examining Old English prose style, its principal practitioners, and their world view.

courses.label: ENGL 305B

noting in representative Old English
poems those things about its purpose.
style, and its audience which make it
unique but which also provide the begin-
nings of the English poetic tradition. Prereq: ENGL 305A

English Language and Linguistics
A study of basic linguistic principles and
concepts, historical and formal. Formerly ENGL 373 and ENGL 375

courses.label: ENGL 306A
courses.title: Introduction to Linguistics
paras: Introduction to linguistics and the principles of linguistic analysis through an examination of English phonology, forms, syntax, and discourse.
Formerly ENGL 375A

courses.label: ENGL 306B
courses.title: Modern English Grammar
paras: Introduction to madern English grammar and structure-its meaningful forms and syntax. Several methods of analysis will be employed and evaluated, including the traditional, structural, transformational-generative, and functional.
Prereq: ENGL 306A Formerly ENGL 375B

courses.label: ENGL 306C
courses.title: Historical Linguistics
paras: Introduction to historical reconstruction and comparative analysis. Basic phonological, morphological, syntactic changes as they manifest themselves in language will be examined.
Prereq: ENGL 306A
Formerly ENGL 373A

courses.label: ENGL 306D
courses.title: The History of English
paras: Introduction to the linguistic history of English from earliest documents to the present, with some consideration of various modern dialects.
Prereq: ENGL 306A
Formerly ENGL 373B

courses.label: ENGL 306E
courses.title: Linguistics and Literatures
paras: A Study of linguistics and its applications in analyzing the style and language of literature. Topics include the relationship between the structure of language and literature, speech and writing, speech arts and genres, discourse and text.

courses.label: ENGL 309A
courses.title: Rhetoric: Principles and Practice 1
paras: A study of various theories of rhetoric. Students are assigned several essays in order to practise and apply the principles of rhetoric to discourse.
Prereq: A 200-level writing course or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 309B
courses.title: Rhetoric: Principles and Practice 2
paras: A continuation of ENGL 309A with an emphasis on the importance of style in rhetorical theory and practice.
Prereq: A 200-level writing course or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 308C
courses.title: Contemporary Rhetorical Theory
paras: An examination of contemporary rhetorical theory and its relationships to criticism, interdisciplinary studies, and computer applications.
Prereq: A 200-level writing course or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 309D
courses.title: Approaches to Style
paras: Theories of style and approaches to the Stylistic analysis of both literary and nonliterary texts. Students will consider contributions to the study of style from such areas as traditional stylistics, New Criticism, formalism, affective stylistics, speech act theory, discourse analysis, and sociolinguistics.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 310A
courses.title: Middie English 1
paras: A study of the minor poems of Chaucer, “The Book of the Duchess,” “Parliament of Fowis,” and “Troilus,” along with related Middle English texts.

courses.label: ENGL 310B
courses.title: Middle English 2
paras: A study of Chaucer’s Canterbury Tales and related Middle English poems and prose.

courses.label: ENGL 312
courses.title: Literature of the Commonwealth
paras: A survey of Australian poetry and prose, with some consideration of the literatures, in English, from Africa and the West Indies.

courses.label: ENGL 313
courses.title: Canadian Literature to 1920
paras: A study of Canadian prose and verse to 1920, with particular attention to the poetry of the School of the Sixties and to the historical and idyllic novels of the 19th and early 20th centuries.

courses.label: ENGL 314
courses.title: Canadian Poetry Since 1920 Poetry in Canada from E.J. Pratt and
paras: A.J.M. Smith to Leonard Cohen.

courses.label: ENGL 315
courses.title: Canadian Prose Since 1920
paras: The Canadian novel since the appearance of Morley Callaghan, with brief consideration of the essay and short story during the period.

courses.label: ENGL 316
courses.title: Canadian Drama
paras: A study of plays by such dramatists as Merrill Denison, Robertson Davies, Gratien Gélinas (in translation), James Reaney, John Coulter, George Ryga, and Michel Tremblay (in translation). Background for 20th-century drama will be provided in lectures..
Cross-listed as DRAMA 351

courses.label: ENGL 325
courses.title: Reading, Leisure, and Human Development
paras: An introduction to the selection and application of literature in Counselling, Recreation, and community settings. Students will be offered theoretical and experiential instruction in a workshopstyle seminar. Assignments will be approximately eight novels or anthologies. A bibliography will be provided. A term paper will be required.

courses.label: ENGL 335
courses.title: Creative Writing 1
paras: Aimed at encouraging students to develop their creative and critical potentials, the course consists of supervised practice, tutorials, and seminar discussions.

courses.label: ENGL 336
courses.title: Creative Writing 2
paras: Designed to assist advanced creative writers to develop their skills in various genres by means of workshop processes, supervised practice, and critical discussion of one or more major projects. .
Prereq: ENGL 335 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 343
courses.title: American Literature |
paras: The meaning of America - the myth, the dream, and the reality - as experienced through its major literary works. Sin, guilt, madness, mysticism, and grace: the search for fulfillment and peace by such writers as Poe, Thoreau, Whitman, Twain, and Crane.

courses.label: ENGL 344
courses.title: Modern American Literature
paras: Approaches to reality amid the confusion and uncertainty of 20th-century America. Emphasis on such major writers as Faulkner, Miller, and Cummings.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 345
courses.title: Studies In American Literature
paras: (Usually only one or two courses from this series are offered each year.)

courses.label: ENGL 345B
courses.title: American Fiction
paras: The Southern Myth: its origins in early literature, its flowering and ruin, as seen by white and black writers, including Twain, Faulkner, Welty, Styron, Grau, O'Connor, Wright, and Ellison.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 346C
courses.title: American Fiction
paras: Special emphasis will be given to the works of two or three major American novelists such as Herman Melville and William Faulkner.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 347A
courses.title: Contemporary American Literature
paras: A study of American Literature from World War 2 to the present.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ENGL 350A
paras: 17th-Century Non-Dramatic Literature 1
A study of secular and religious lyric poetry by poets such as Donne, Jonson, Herrick, Herbert, Vaughan, and Marvell.

courses.label: ENGL 350B
paras: 17th-Century Non-Dramatic Literature 2
A study of selected prose works of Bacon, Burton, and Browne. A more intensive study of Milton’s English poetry and a selection of his prose works.

courses.label: ENGL 362
courses.title: Shakespeare 1
paras: A study of the plays written before 1599-1600, excluding Julius Caesar.

courses.label: ENGL 363
courses.title: Shakespeare 2
paras: A study of the plays written after 1599-1600, including Julius Caesar.

courses.label: ENGL 365
courses.title: Selected Studies
paras: Designed to provide a study in depth of problems and/or authors selected by the instructor. Students interested in initiating such courses are encouraged to do so by bringing their ideas to the attention of individual instructors.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.title: Writing for Special Purposes 1
paras: and 2 Each term will consist of three or four units on such topics as editing; magazine, newspaper, and editorial writing; advertising and public relations writing; instructional manuals; interpretation of specialized information for general audiences; writing for non-print media; ethics in writing; etc. Substantial use will be made of non-academic experts in the fields covered.

courses.label: ENGL 410A
courses.title: Satire and Sense: The Restoration and Early 18th Century
paras: The Restoration comedy of manners, heroic and high tragedy, poetry of the court wits and other amused commentators on society, and the major writings of Dryden, Swift, Addison, Defoe, and the early Pope.

courses.label: ENGL 410B
courses.title: Sense and Sensibility: The Middle and Later 18th Century
paras: The probing of mores and manners by Pope and Johnson, the emergence of the novel with Fielding and Sterne, and the transformation {in “the age of sensibility’) of literary attitudes and practice from classical to romanticism.

courses.label: ENGL 430A
courses.title: The Romantic Movement 1
paras: The poetry and critical theory of Blake, Wordsworth, and Coleridge. Emphasis is primarily on poetry; selected minor writers may be considered.

courses.label: ENGL 430B
courses.title: The Romantic Movement 2
paras: The poetry and critical theory of Byron, Shelley and Keats. Emphasis is primarily on poetry; selected minor writers may be considered.

courses.label: ENGL 451A
courses.title: Literature of the Victorian Age 1
paras: An historical and critical study of major poets (Browning, Tennyson, Arnold) and of the literary criticism of the period.

courses.label: ENGL 451B
courses.title: Literature of the Victorian Age 2
paras: An historical and critical study of major novelists (Dickens, Thackeray, Eliot) and major essayists (Newman, Ruskin, Mill, Huxley).

courses.label: ENGL 460A
courses.title: British Literature, 1885-1914
paras: A study of works by such writers as Shaw, Conrad, and Yeats.

will be feminist criticism, Marxist criticism.
psychoanalytic criticism and, especially, deconstruction.

courses.label: ERS 100
courses.title: Issue Analysis and Problem Solving for Environmental Studies 1
paras: Designed to complement the introductory overview of ENV S 195 and the introduction to methods and techniques (ERS 150). Selected themes and case examples are analyzed within a framework of concepts and theories from the natural and social sciences. Students undertake practical exercises to develop analytic and problem-solving skills.
Prereq: Honours Environment and Resource Studies students only

courses.label: ERS 101
courses.title: Issue Analysis and Problem Solving for Environmental Studies 2
paras: Continuation of ERS 100.
Prereq: Honours Environment and Resource Studies students only

courses.label: ERS 150
courses.title: Environmental issues: Methods and Techniques
paras: Course will teach basic research skills to complement the problem-solving skills taught in ERS 100/101. Concentration on the “systems approach” and its use in problem solving, with attention to information gathering and organization, quantitative data analysis techniques, and presentation skills. Microcomputers will be used for report generation, information organization and basic data analysis. Prereq: Honours Environment and Resource Studies students only or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 218
courses.title: Introduction to Canadian Energy issues
paras: Emphasis on physical concepts, terminology, units, current policy, supply and demand noting technical and economic aspects, and alternative energy strategies.

courses.label: ERS 220
courses.title: Introduction to Envire tal Economics
paras: Introduction to the history of economic thought and the various schools of economic thought as these relate to environmental cases, issues and analysis.

courses.label: ERS 231
courses.title: Environmental Issues in a Global Perspective
paras: This course examines the various political, economic and social factors in development and environmental concerns in various Third World countries. Special focus is on health-care systems, agricultural and forestry practices and policies, water management and resource ownership. Students are encouraged to study one country in some depth, and to submit seminars and projects.
Prereq: Second year or above

courses.label: ERS 241
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Social impact Assessment
paras: An introduction to means of assessing proposed approaches to environmentally and socially significant problems and opportunities. Special emphasis on the nature and limitations of conventional means of assessing the impacts, and overall desirability of technologies, projects, plans and policies. Close examination of case examples.

courses.label: ERS 275A
courses.title: Special Readings
paras: Background reading and study in consultation with Faculty. Typically utilized when a student must study a topic in connection with other work, but no course offering that topic is available. Prereq: Consent of instructor The letter designation allows this course to be taken more than once for credit

courses.label: ERS 290
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Individual or small group project emphasizing multidisciplinary treatment of environmental problems. Wark encouraged on situations of interest to community organizations, government agencies or other groups.
Prereq: Environment and Resource Studies students only

courses.label: ERS 291
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Continuation of project begun in ERS 290 Prereq: ERS 290

courses.label: ERS 295
courses.title: Development of Environmental Thought 1
paras: Examination of conflicting positions on how we do and should view the natural world and ourselves, beginning with review of the history of attitudes to the environment and our place in it. Emphasis on evolution of attitudes to human nature and the environment in industrial society, critiques of these attitudes and implications for approaches to modern environmental issues.
Prereq: Environment and Resource Studies students only or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 305
courses.title: Ecosystem Perspectives and
paras: Analyses : Examination of the concept of the “ecosystem” presented in recent writings about non-equilibrium thermodynamics, ecological paradigms, conservation biology and environmental philosophy. Discussion of the theoretical and practical implications of these contrasting perspectives for issues of research/ environmental management and sustainable development.

courses.label: ERS 318
courses.title: Soft Energy Paths in Canada
paras: Analysis and evaluation of energy strategies based on energy conservation and renewable energy systems, Technical, economic, ecological, and social aspects will be examined.
Prereq: ERS 218 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 320
courses.title: Environmental Economics
paras: Evaluation of various economic approaches to the environment. Introduction to various models used to analyse . environmental quality and used in the design of environmental policy and management initiatives.
Prereq: ERS 220 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 337
courses.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
paras: Major problems and issues in the management of environmental impacts stemming from development projects. Synthesis of ecological, economic-and institutional aspects . Integrating environmental management with social and economic development policies and programs.
Prereq: ERS 241 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 338

introductory Note

There are a number of courses offered in the Facuity of Environmental Studies of an integrative nature which extend across the academic interests of the four units: School of Architecture, Department of Geography, Department of Environ ment and Resource Studies, and Schooi of Urban and Regional Planning. The courses are of a general interest and are open to ail students in the University. There is not an actual Department of Environmental Studies. Students interested in this area are urged to consult the course offerings of the four individual units mentioned above. These four departments/schools offer a variety of rélated courses allowing in depth studies of topics covered in the Environmental Studies courses.

courses.label: ENVS 178
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Research Methods
paras: Introduction to methods of developing, evaluating and using evidence in Environmental Studies. Methods for summarizing and critical appreciation of data describing environmental systems. Skilt development in applying statistical techniques and in using microcomputers as a research tool.
Prereq: CS 100 or high school computing course or consent of instructor
Students may receive credit for only one of ENV S 178 and PSYCH 292, STAT 202, 204, 205, 210, 220

courses.label: ENVS 195
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
paras: Theories, methods and concepts in study of the environment. Emphasis on natural and built environment and relationships between elements of the environment. Environmental planning, management, and design discussed.

courses.label: ENVS 200
courses.title: Field Ecology
paras: Introduces the main concepts and principles of ecology; the cycling of elements; energetics and structural organization of major ecological systems; population dynamics; impact of natural resource management practices and urban and industrial development on the environment; incorporating environmental quality considerations into development activities. The laboratory sessions include field trips to study natural and disturbed ecosystems, urban and applied ecology. Prereq: Second, third and fourth year students only Lab fee of $5

courses.label: ENVS 201
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Planning Law
paras: introduction to legal concepts generally and to environmental and planning law concepts in particular. Designed both for
Students who do not plan to take further

in depth legal courses and as a prerequisite for senior legal courses - ENV S 401 and ENV S 402. Topics to be covered include Sources of Law, Nature of Legal Remedies, Common Law, Judicial Review, Administrative Agencies and the law retating to them, Planning Act, Environmental Protection and Assessment Acts, and Federal Fisheries Act.

courses.label: ENVS 202
courses.title: Social Science Approaches to Environmental Problems —
paras: Research strategies for understanding and addressing environmental problem/ opportunity situations based on concepts and methods derived from the social and behavioural sciences. Particular attention is given to determining the appropriate mix of research strategies for a range of situations in terms of data validity and reliability, time and financial constraints, and ethical considerations.
Prereq: Second-year students or consent of instructor.

Course Descriptions

FIRST-YEAR COURSES

1. The Department reserves the right to refuse admission to, and/or credit for, any of its language courses to a student who has, in the view of the Department, a level of competence unsuited to that course.

2. Students with some elementary or secondary school French not exceeding Year Two (Ontario Grade 10) should enrol in French 151. Those with secondary school Year Three (Ontario Grade 11) should enrol in French 152.
3. Students with secondary school Year Four French (Ontario Grade 12) or equivalent should enrol in French 155.
4. Students with Grade 13 secondary school French should enrol in French 192A/B and/or French 195/196.
5. Students may enrol only in courses for which they have secondary school antirequisites with the written permission of the Department of French.

6. All students intending to register in any University of Waterloo French language course at the 100 level (FR 151, 182, 155, 192A, 192B) who have secondary school Year Five (Ontario Grade 13) French or equivalent must take the French Lanaguage Placement Test to be held on Thursday, September 10, 1987 at 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. in Arts Lecture Hall 116.
7. Students should consult the Departmental brochure "French at Waterloo" for further details, and for any changes in offerings after the Calendar goes to press.
8. Linguistics, Language, Civilization, and Literature courses are listed separately below.

courses.label: GENE 351
courses.title: Information Technology and Society
paras: The social and technological concepts of an information society. Overview of information technology; current states and future directions in computers and communications. Study of an information system, its promises and problems including privacy, security, user acceptance, retraining, control, etc. Impact of information technology on the quality of life; employment, freedom of information, leisure, creativity, etc. One application area will be selected for study each term from Computer-Aided Learning, Office Automation, Computer-Aided Design and Manufacturing, Telecomputing, etc. Prereq: Open to third- or fourth-year Students in any faculty with at least one university-level computing course, or consent of the instructor

courses.title: Technical Entrepreneurship
paras: Technical entrepreneurship is examined considering the role of independent business, entrepreneurial behaviour, types of business and enterprises, business structure, sources of venture concepts and capital, company operation and control, and business start-up.
Prereq: A course in Engineering Economics (or equivalent)

courses.title: Engineering Law
paras: General introduction of Law and Common Law Legal Systems; Formation of Contracts, Effect of mistakes on Contracts, Interpretation of Contracts.
Breach of Contracts, Legal Remedies.

Scope and content of technical specifications; Sale of goods; introduction of the Law of Agency; the Tort of Negligence, Professional Negligence; some aspects of Restrictive Trade Practices; Introduction to Patent Law. Ethical aspects of professional practice.
Restricted to fourth-year Chemical, Computer/Electrical and Systems Design Engineering Students

courses.label: GENE 412
courses.title: Ethics and The Engineering Profession
paras: An application of philosophical analysis and theories of ethics to issues of moral conduct in the engineering profession. Discussions will include such matters as the social responsibilities of engineers, standards of product safety and liability, the assessment of acceptable risk, conflicts of interest and obligation, professional loyalty and “whistle
blowing", use and enforcement of profes
sional codes of ethics, the
“democratization” of the profession, and
the moral implications of technology. Not open to Year One students. Cross-listed as PHIL 315

courses.label: GENE 460
courses.title: Orthopaedic Bioengineering
paras: Introduction of engineering technology to the field of orthopaedics. Specific topics deal with the repair and reconstruction of portions of the musculoskeletal system affected by trauma or pathological response. Primary study is directed toward the skeletal joints and major load carrying structure.

Prereq: Students must have background study in properties and mechanics of materials equivalent to CIV E 204 and ClV E 265. Registration in this course will be assessed on an individual basis through scheduled interviews.
Cross-listed as CIV E 460
